title: 50-day unattended run hardening
summary: Hardened the 50-day unattended-run paths for completed-manifest JSONL appends, pending-publish bounded scans, completed-history reads, queue/diagnostics payload caps, desktop log rotation, source-scan cache preservation, and close-readiness during stop requests.
reason: The unattended-run audit found concrete long-run failure modes where normal UI/API refreshes or concurrent local worker slots could corrupt evidence, grow payloads without bound, hide active stopping work, or replace last-good queue evidence with misleading empty state.
behavior_before: Completed-job manifest appends were not locked under local worker slots; deferred pending-publish startup read every manifest; limited completed-history reads loaded the whole JSONL; queue and diagnostics summaries could grow or scan without a hard cap; source scan timeouts could overwrite last-good cache evidence; desktop API logs did not rotate; StopRequested progress could be treated as safe to close.
behavior_after: Completed-job manifest appends use the shared JSONL mutex and report append failures; deferred pending-publish startup writes aggregate evidence without per-manifest reads; limited completed-history reads use a bounded tail reader; queue snapshots and diagnostics directory summaries expose capped/sampled evidence; timed-out/stopped/error source scans preserve the last-good cache; desktop API logs rotate; active stopping progress blocks close-readiness until terminal evidence.

That restores unlocked completed-manifest appends, full deferred pending-publish summary reads, full-file completed-history limited reads, uncapped queue/diagnostics summaries, prior source-cache overwrite behavior, non-rotating desktop API log handling, and previous StopRequested close-readiness policy.
